title: Falsification of import-closure-only behavioral-oracle reuse
hypothesis: Over at least 200 Git revision comparisons across three previously unused Python repositories, a statically recovered import-only source closure predicts all changes in independent observable oracles (zero false reuse decisions) while saving at least 50% of oracle execution time including indexing overhead.

repos.oracle: import blinker.Signal; connect a strong callback; send and record returned receiver values, not just a test's pass/fail
import public Encoder and Decoder; encode and decode fixed HTTP/2 header tuples; record encoded bytes and decoded values
import public Frame and DataFrame; serialize fixed DATA frame; decode frame header and body; record bytes and decoded payload

comparison: Each of 70 consecutive first-parent historical revisions per repo is compared with its pinned HEAD, for 210 candidate comparisons; no changed-source candidate is removed on the basis of results. In addition, a syntactically valid local-only adversarial change to package __init__.py is applied to each repo after the pinned HEAD; source-module graph itself is not altered.
static_predictor: AST-declared production imports reachable from the focus module in the pinned HEAD (direct imports and relative imports), exact pinned Git blob identity of those source module paths; does not infer implicit package initializer runtime edges or other side effects. A missing tracked module forces REFUSE, not reuse.
decision: REUSE if all tracked module paths have identical Git blobs; otherwise REVERIFY; any unsupported version or oracle failure is classified UNASSESSABLE, not silently counted correct.

adversarial_mutations.operation: append monkeypatch Signal.send to return an empty list
append monkeypatch Encoder.encode to return empty encoded bytes
append monkeypatch DataFrame.serialize to return nine zero bytes

oracle_comparison: Use a fresh isolated CPython 3.13 process per checked revision. Compare deterministic, canonically encoded JSON behavioral observations; don't count an import error as a changed successful behavior. This tests observed behavior, not normative correctness.
miss: An observed successful oracle output differs between pinned revision and target while the predictor says REUSE. Any one miss falsifies the no-misses prediction for the tested scope.
timing: Measure total control oracle subprocess time for assessable target revisions. Counterfactual experiment cost = wall clock static index computation + target oracle time for REVERIFY decisions. Report both and sampling limitations. Do not combine results across repositories without per-repo figures.
success_rule: Only if all 210 historical comparisons are assessable, three adversarial cases are assessable, zero missed changes and >=50% verification time saved.
failure_rule: One valid miss suffices to falsify the no-misses prediction regardless of how many history comparisons are assessable. Under 50% savings also falsifies the economic requirement only when timing sample is complete.
limitations: Only the explicitly specified import-only predictor is being challenged; richer semantic dependency models may behave differently.
Historical behavior changes may be intentional, so this studies oracle-observation preservation rather than whether those changes were regressions.
Code from untrusted public repositories executes in an isolated ephemeral CI runner, not the local ChatGPT sandbox.
The fixed oracle set is not complete behavioral coverage and no zero-miss result could prove universal soundness.
Generated mutation branches remain local to runner and are never pushed.
